intro: Acute Severe Asthma Management is an in-app clinical reference guide for status asthmaticus in children, covering the first-line drug trio and escalation therapies. It organizes treatment into three core medication classes — β2 agonists, anticholinergic agents, and corticosteroids — plus a set of escalation medications for refractory cases. The guide also includes clinical pearls on severity assessment, IV magnesium as a preferred first escalation step, and indications for intubation. Per the source, the research-based context in these pearls draws on the GINA 2023 Global Strategy for Asthma Management, the BTS/SIGN British Asthma Guideline 2019, and AAP Section on Pulmonology consensus.
indications: Guiding first-line drug selection (β2 agonist, anticholinergic, corticosteroid) for a child in acute severe asthma / status asthmaticus
Assessing severity using criteria such as ability to speak, respiratory rate, heart rate, oxygen saturation, and peak flow
Selecting an escalation agent when first-line therapy is insufficient
Deciding when a child in status asthmaticus needs intubation and planning a rapid sequence induction approach
Reviewing dosing and administration notes for each medication class at the bedside
method: The guide presents medications grouped into three core classes — β2 agonist, anticholinergic agents, and corticosteroids — each with its own dosing and frequency notes, followed by an "Other medications" escalation section (magnesium, theophylline, ketamine, vecuronium). It is a structured reference rather than a calculator: there is no computed score, only a fixed set of medication and severity-assessment information transcribed from the source guide, supplemented with labelled "research add-on" clinical pearls.

faqs.q: What three drug classes make up first-line therapy in this guide?
faqs.a: β2 agonists, anticholinergic agents, and corticosteroids, presented under the guide's "Medications" section.

faqs.q: What escalation medications are listed for refractory status asthmaticus?
faqs.a: Magnesium, theophylline, ketamine, and vecuronium are listed under "Other medications."

faqs.q: What severity criteria does the guide reference?
faqs.a: A GINA 2023-sourced pearl lists criteria including inability to speak in full sentences, respiratory rate over 30/min with accessory muscle use, heart rate over 120/min, SpO2 under 90% on room air, and PEF at or below 50% of predicted/personal best.

faqs.q: What is the guide's preferred escalation step after standard therapy fails?
faqs.a: A clinical pearl in the guide identifies IV magnesium as the preferred escalation after about one hour of standard therapy without improvement.

faqs.q: What guidelines inform the research add-on pearls in this guide?
faqs.a: The source cites the GINA Global Strategy for Asthma Management 2023, the BTS/SIGN British Asthma Guideline 2019, and AAP Section on Pulmonology consensus.
